description: We are building Field Shift, a global farm advisor for the Adapting Farms with NASA Data challenge. Pick any field on Earth and it turns NASA POWER rainfall, temperature, soil moisture and sunlight into a weekly plan: when to irrigate, sow or protect crops, with drought, flood, heat and frost risk. Looking for people skilled in agriculture, Earth science, data analysis, web development, design, and ML to help refine, test and present it. Join us!
summary: AgriNaut is a free web app that turns NASA satellite and model data into a weekly farming plan for any location on Earth. A farmer clicks a point on the map or searches a place, chooses a crop, and the app retrieves recent rainfall, temperature, soil moisture and sunlight from NASA POWER. It estimates crop water use and a 14-day water balance, scores drought, flood, heat and frost risk, and gives plain-language advice in English, Urdu and Spanish: irrigate now, hold irrigation, delay sowing, or protect against cold. It also ranks seven crops for the chosen place and tells the farmer roughly how much water a field of their size will need. An analytics tab shows trends, distributions and correlations. AgriNaut addresses the challenge by helping farms adapt to changing weather using open NASA data that is otherwise hard for farmers to use directly.
details:
What it does: AgriNaut is an interactive farm advisor. Users pick any location (map click, drag the pin, place search, or quick picks), choose one of seven crops, set their field size, and receive a conditions score from 0 to 100 plus a prioritized weekly plan.

How it works: For the chosen point the app requests daily NASA POWER data for the last 30 to 90 days: corrected precipitation, maximum and minimum air temperature, root-zone soil wetness and surface sunlight. From these I calculate reference evapotranspiration with a radiation-based Hargreaves-type formula, crop water use using crop coefficients, a 14-day water balance, growing degree days, irrigation volume per hectare and for the whole field, and four risk scores (drought, flood, heat, frost). Rule-based logic converts these into advice and checks the sowing season by hemisphere. An analytics tab shows statistics, trends, distributions and correlations for each variable. The map uses NASA GIBS imagery, including MODIS vegetation and GPM IMERG rain overlays for context.

Benefits and impact: It helps farmers decide when to irrigate, sow or protect crops, saving water and reducing crop loss, in three languages.

Tools: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Leaflet maps, NASA POWER API, NASA GIBS.

Creativity: The app works globally instead of for one region, compares seven crops for the chosen place, adapts sowing seasons for the southern hemisphere, and uses NASA’s own imagery as the base map so it still loads where other map services are blocked.

Factors considered: Farmers need plain-language advice rather than raw data; internet access and language vary, so the interface is multilingual and lightweight; and data limits matter. NASA POWER covers a grid cell of about 50 km, arrives about 3 days late, and soil wetness is modeled. Crop thresholds are general estimates, so the advice is decision support, not a replacement for local agronomists.

Demo note: The demo video is an animated walkthrough of the interface with sample values, not a screen recording. The working app is live at https://zuni005.github.io/Agrinaut/ and retrieves real NASA POWER data when used.

SI use: This project was developed by Zunairah Shaikh, who chose the challenge, defined the features and requirements, tested the live app, deployed it on GitHub Pages and prepared this submission though i took help at some points from AI Agents for github mainly and formatting.
